speaker: Doctor
text: That will be all for now. To begin our assessment, please tell me: where exactly are you experiencing the most significant imbalance, and did you have any recent infections or changes in your vision?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for clarifying that the symptoms are predominantly on the right side. Have you noticed any changes in your vision, such as double vision or blurred vision, and do you have a history of stroke, diabetes, or high blood pressure?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML).

Based on your history of Crohn's disease and one year of natalizumab use, combined with your new onset of unilateral ataxia and "drunk" gait, you are at high risk for JC virus reactivation. I need to confirm the extent of CNS involvement. REQUEST IMAGES: Brain_MRI_with_contrast.
